findings.message: Adopted P/E/H proofs are re-validated against volatile live evidence instead of their frozen identities, creating an unrecoverable record. validateIntegrationProofs() -> validateAdoptedArtifact() -> validateArtifactPending() calls assertEvidenceReady(record,{finalized:true}) for every adopted report/closure/handoff proof, and withRecord() runs validateIntegrationProofs() before every mutation. Trigger A: after report-adopt (or close-adopt), run integrate-gate/integrate-review/integrate-verify once; invalidateFinalization() sets evidence.finalized=false and the write succeeds (validateRecord() does not re-run proof validation), but every subsequent command (including integrate-finalize) fails in the pre-mutate validation with 'integration evidence finalization identity is missing or stale'. Trigger B: resume after P in a process whose inherited environment differs at all (environmentHandle() in gates.mjs hashes the entire process.env except _, SHLVL, OLDPWD, e.g. PWD/TERM_SESSION_ID), so assertEvidenceReady() reports 'fresh integration gate is missing or failed' inside the read-time validation and no command can proceed; gates cannot be re-run because the mutation path is blocked first. Impact: story cannot reach E/H through the tool; only manual JSON edits of the unauthenticated record recover it, which contradicts the AC2 fresh-process interruption/resume claim and AC3 P->E ordering. Fix: validate adopted proofs against stored identities (effective_review_identity, gate identities, stored env hash) rather than live conditions, and refuse evidence mutations once report.commit or closure.commit is set.

No re-prepare or abandon path once an integration record exists. prepareLocalIntegration() returns the existing record from the fs.existsSync(file) branch keyed solely by run id: a 'failed' probe record is returned forever even after the integration branch is updated to resolve the conflict, and a 'prepared' record whose base I has advanced fails with 'prepared integration base is no longer current' with no supported way to re-probe against the new I. Since the PM has standing authority to merge other stories/upstream changes into I between prepare and adopt, this is a realistic dead end that requires manually deleting .deliver/integrations/<run>.json. Design recommendation, not a false-PASS defect: add an explicit supersede/re-prepare operation that archives the prior probe/preparation.

Whole-checkout proofs spawn one git subprocess per tracked blob and are recomputed several times per command. fingerprintBlob() runs `git cat-file blob <oid>` per entry; checkoutObjectEntries() walks `ls-tree -r <commit>` for the entire tree ('.'), and per command withRecord()->validateIntegrationProofs() validates the base I proof and the adopted M proof, then assertExecutableM()->executableProof()->verifyCheckoutProof()->validateCheckoutProofObjects() walks the tree again plus liveFingerprint() of every file; runIntegrationGate() does this twice more. On a repository with thousands of files each integrate-* command costs tens of thousands of process spawns. Recommendation (performance/design, not correctness): use the Git blob oid as the committed identity and `git cat-file --batch`/`hash-object --stdin-paths` for live comparison, and validate frozen proofs by hash rather than full recomputation.

Two worktrees are mandatory and the source checkout must stay parked at C on the story branch until handoff H is adopted: assertRecordSource() fails with 'finished source checkout no longer remains at C' if HEAD/branch of state.project_root move, and prepareLocalIntegration() requires branch(sourceRoot)===pm_binding.branch while branch(integrationRoot)===integrationBranch, so the same directory can never serve both roles. This blocks starting the next story in the source checkout until P/E/H complete. Acceptable if documented as the sequential-delivery contract (shipping.md not supplied), otherwise an autonomy restriction worth relaxing by binding immutable C via object identity instead of checkout position.

`--verification-report` is silently dropped for tiny/small scales: prepareLocalIntegration() computes reportingRequested = scale==='standard' && verificationReport===true, so an explicit user request on a tiny/small project yields reporting 'skipped' with no error or diagnostic. Either honor the request or fail loudly.

Reuse and proof scope are stricter than the acceptance text implies and will frequently force fresh evidence or gate failure. (1) source_reusable requires the live completion snapshot (which includes ignored/untracked files under touches, per scope.mjs snapshotVersion) to equal committed C, so any build cache or coverage output inside a touched directory at finish makes C review non-reusable. (2) protectedIgnoredEntries() includes every ignored path matching (config|configs|contract|contracts) such as node_modules/**/config.js, so a gate that installs/updates dependencies fails verifyCheckoutProof() with 'protected Git metadata changed'. Both are inherited from scope.mjs protectedIgnored; conservative rather than wrong, but worth narrowing for practical autonomy.

parseReviewReceipt() validates top-level `findings` when a `panel` is present but then discards them, returning only member-derived findings. A receipt that lists a finding at top level without attributing it to a member loses it silently. Require top-level findings to be empty or identical to the derived set when a panel is supplied.

Small robustness/format issues: handoffContent() hardcodes budget denominators 'rounds x/3 · retries y/2' instead of deriving them from the recorded policy; prepareLocalIntegration()'s `merge-base --is-ancestor` try/catch treats any git failure as 'not an ancestor'; buildCheckoutProof() fails with 'initialized submodule is absent from expected M' when C removes a submodule still initialized in I (requires manual deinit) and raises a raw git error when the integration submodule clone lacks M's gitlink object instead of a 'fetch the submodule first' message.

summary: Design assessment: the C/I/M/P/E/H model is sound and largely serves the plan. Strengths verified in the supplied code: adoptLocalIntegration()/recheckM() enforce the exact no-ff I+C topology and merge-tree composition, integration gates run only the source-declared commands at actual M, reusability is limited to clean composition with identical bound manifests and recomputed on every read, effectiveEvidence() requires fresh M review and verification when inputs drift without touching C, distinct-verifier separation is enforced both at source (state.mjs patch, including panel members) and at M, P is required between M and E for large/regulated with exact paths and no self-referential hash, adoptArtifacts() bounds each commit to its prepared paths and bytes, closure retains owner/rounds/retries via replaceStoryExecution(), handoff uses closure E as BASE_COMMIT with H as its own handoff-only commit, and panel receipts retain member identities/verdicts/findings with legacy receipts still accepted. Actual bugs: the block finding (frozen P/E/H proofs revalidated against volatile finalized flag and live environment hash, producing an unrecoverable record after a post-P gate rerun or an environment change on resume) undermines AC2/AC3; the two majors are design/autonomy gaps (no re-prepare path; per-blob subprocess proofs). Known pending work, not counted as defects: T05C correction runs (source findings remain unresolved by design here), T11 risk-to-panel lens selection (coverage is only enforced at reporting time), T08 resume/doctor, T12 parallel lifecycle, and T14 documentation. Limitations: deliver.mjs, pm.mjs, shipping.md, compatibility.md and operations.json were not supplied, so CLI wiring, the 'finish leaves claim active' runtime behaviour and documentation of the dual-worktree contract could only be judged via the supplied tests; the '153/153 tests passed' claim and the untested combined root+overlay tree were not verified by this review.
